table.title: [val][adversarial] Long group header over tiny sub-columns
table.html:

understanding.purpose: Compare multilingual benchmark accuracy across three model sizes while providing practical notes about each model.
understanding.reading: Readers scan each model row across EN, ZH and AR, compare scores down each language column, and consult the notes for context.
groups: EN, ZH and AR are parallel accuracy measures under one benchmark header, so they should have equal widths.
Model identifies each row; Notes provides supporting prose for the same model.
may_wrap: The long benchmark group header can wrap across its three columns.
Notes can wrap at word boundaries; their wrapping can use row height created by other cells.

preferred.name: r2B
preferred.note: Give Notes more room while keeping the model names intact and testing whether a 270px score group can retain the two-line heading.

acceptable.name: r1A
acceptable.note: Give the benchmark group 30px more than r0B while retaining a wide Notes column and using the full available width. This tests whether the header can improve without substantially increasing note wrapping.

acceptable.name: r1B
acceptable.note: Give the benchmark header a wider span while keeping Notes wider than in r0A. This tests a balance between a shorter header and compact prose rows.

acceptable.name: r1C
acceptable.note: Use the unused width in r0B and give a little more space to both the benchmark group and Notes. This preserves its compact body while testing whether the header wraps more comfortably.

acceptable.name: r2A
acceptable.note: Reduce Model slightly and test narrower equal score columns while returning space to Notes. This may preserve the two-line group heading and improve the first note's line lengths.

acceptable.name: r2C
acceptable.note: Give the benchmark heading a little more room for a more relaxed two-line setting, while checking whether the narrower Notes column still keeps the long note to two lines.

acceptable.name: r3A
acceptable.note: Test a midpoint between r2A and r2C: give the score group a little more presence while preserving a generous Notes measure and some breathing room for model names.

acceptable.name: r3B
acceptable.note: Test a more compact score group to give the first note a longer measure. Check whether the benchmark heading still wraps gracefully across the narrower group.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: The benchmark header would wrap into several short lines above three disproportionately narrow score columns, while Notes would receive much more space than its text needs.
bad.why: The benchmark header would wrap into several short lines above three disproportionately narrow score columns, while Notes would receive much more space than its text needs.

rationale: r2B gives the three comparable language scores equal widths and enough combined space for the group header to read in two balanced lines. Notes remains wide enough for the longer entries to read comfortably, and the model names stay intact. The alternatives with narrower score columns are publishable, though their three-line group header makes the header block taller without improving the body rows.

general: Give parallel measures a consistent visual rhythm so readers can compare them easily.
Allocate space to spanning headers as well as individual cells; a group label can determine the useful minimum width of its columns.
Judge wrapping by its effect on hierarchy and reading, not by line count alone.
specific: The long benchmark label needs substantially more combined width than the two-digit scores beneath it.
Notes benefits from the remaining width, but its longest entry still wraps to two lines in the preferred design.

tradeoffs: Wider score columns make the group header more spacious but take room from Notes; narrower score columns give the prose more room at the cost of a taller header.
uncertain: A designer might prefer r2A or r3A for a little more breathing room around the scores. The ranges are approximate, with the three score columns kept equal and widths adjusted together within the viewport; individual endpoints are not intended to be combined independently.

critique.good: The benchmark header fits in two lines, and the equal score columns make the three languages easy to compare. Model names and values remain intact.
critique.problems: The Small note takes three lines and the Large note takes two, making those rows tall beside mostly empty score cells.
critique.cause: The 319px Notes column is relatively narrow, while each short score value receives a 105px column.

critique.good: The wide Notes column keeps the Small note to two lines and the Large note to one. Equal score columns preserve the parallel structure, and all model names and values remain intact.
critique.problems: The benchmark header takes three lines, creating a tall header above short language labels. A small strip of viewport width remains unused.
critique.cause: The three 75px score columns give the spanning header only 225px, while the widths total 699px.

critique.good: The benchmark header fits in two lines, and the equal score columns clearly express the language comparison.
critique.problems: The Small note takes four lines and the Large note takes two, producing tall rows and conspicuous empty space under the scores.
critique.cause: The three 135px score columns consume space that the prose needs, leaving only 224px for Notes.

critique.good: The three equal score columns make language comparisons straightforward, and the notes remain legible without splitting words. Each model row reads as a unit.
critique.problems: The benchmark heading occupies three lines and makes the header disproportionately tall, while the score columns contain considerable empty space.
critique.cause: The three 85px score columns give the spanning heading too little width to fit on two lines; the 389px Notes column takes more space than is needed to keep the longest note to two lines.

critique.good: The benchmark heading fits on two lines, giving the header a more balanced height. Equal score columns support comparison, and both longer notes fit comfortably without splitting words.
critique.problems: The score columns are wider than their short values need, while the long first note wraps fairly close to the right edge. The 75px Model column also has a little spare room.
critique.cause: Each score column is 95px wide to accommodate the spanning heading; that width comes from the space available for Notes.

critique.good: The generous Notes column gives the prose room, and equal score columns retain a consistent comparison rhythm.
critique.problems: The benchmark heading breaks into three lines, creating a tall header; the extra Notes width does not reduce the longest note below two lines.
critique.cause: The three 80px score columns constrain the spanning heading, while the 404px Notes column receives width that produces no visible reduction in row height.

critique.good: The three equal score columns read as a coherent comparison group. Model names and scores remain intact, and the notes wrap cleanly. The benchmark heading occupies two lines.
critique.problems: The notes column dominates the table, while the score columns have ample space around their short values. The first note wraps onto a short second line.
critique.cause: The 373px Notes column receives more than half the available width; each score column is 92px wide despite containing only short labels and values.

critique.good: Equal score columns preserve the comparison rhythm, and the wider Notes column gives the prose a comfortable measure. All content remains intact and the heading stays at two lines.
critique.problems: The model column is tight against its longest name, and the first note still requires two lines despite the extra width. The large Notes area makes the score group feel comparatively compressed.
critique.cause: At 66px, Model has only 45px of text space, matching the stated width of its longest word. The 386px Notes column takes space from the score group without reducing the row count.

critique.good: The score group has a more generous, balanced presence, with equal columns that make comparisons easy. The heading and notes wrap without splitting words, and the row heights match the other designs.
critique.problems: The first note has a more balanced two-line wrap, but the narrower Notes column leaves less room for its prose. The score columns contain substantial unused space.
critique.cause: The three 100px score columns take 24px more in total than in r2A, leaving 349px for Notes.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

contrast.why: The notes read comfortably, but the benchmark heading wraps across five lines above three cramped columns, making the header disproportionately tall.

ref_auto.why: The benchmark heading and equal language columns scan clearly, though the narrower notes column adds a line to the Large row.

r1B.why: The two-line group heading sits over evenly sized language columns, while the notes have enough room to keep the Large row on one line.

r1A.why: The language columns and notes are well balanced, but the group heading breaks across three lines, including a split at held-out.

r2B.why: The group heading fits in two lines, the language columns are evenly spaced, and the notes remain easy to read with little wrapping.

ref_equal.why: Wide model and language columns leave the notes squeezed into short lines, producing very tall rows and making comparisons harder.

raw.unsure: C and E are close; the slightly different balance between language columns and notes is a matter of preference.

ref_equal.why: The three numeric columns and Model take up much of the width, leaving Notes so narrow that sentences break into many short lines and make the data rows unnecessarily tall.

contrast.why: Notes reads comfortably, but the benchmark group is cramped: its heading wraps into five lines above three very narrow numeric columns.

r2B.why: The benchmark heading fits in two lines, the three scores have balanced widths, and Notes has enough room for a readable two-line sentence and a single-line final note.

ref_auto.why: The heading and scores are clear, but the wider numeric columns leave less room for Notes, making the final note wrap onto a second line.

r1B.why: The heading fits in two lines, the three score columns are evenly spaced, and Notes is wide enough to keep the final note on one line.

r1A.why: Notes and the scores read clearly, though the benchmark heading takes three lines and leaves a taller header than in C or E.

raw.unsure: C and E are very close; their small differences in column proportions do not produce a clear reading advantage.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
